kurz: More flavour comes from roasted aromas, concentration, acid and salt in the right balance, not from more spice.
bild_im_kopf: Like a mixing desk: salt, acid, sweetness, bitterness and [[umami|umami]] have to suit each other.
bedeutung: Flavour has several layers: roasted aromas from the [[maillard-reaktion|Maillard reaction]], concentration through reducing, seasoning from salt, freshness from acid and depth from umami (cheese, tomato, stock, mushrooms).
was_passiert: A flat dish often needs acid rather than salt. Roasted aromas form when frying, not when boiling. Reducing concentrates everything.
faustregeln: Sear well and deglaze the browned bits.
Season at the end with acid and salt.
